name: Massaman Beef Curry
desc: Oven-braised beef chuck finished in a rich massaman coconut curry with potatoes, carrots, tamarind and peanuts.

source.title: Massaman Beef Curry
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp massaman curry paste (Mae Ploy preferred)
2.5 lb beef chuck roast, fat trimmed, cut into bite-size cubes
ingredients.prep: fat trimmed, cut into bite-size cubes

ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 (19 oz) cans coconut cream or full-fat coconut milk, divided
ingredients.item: coconut cream or full-fat coconut milk

ingredients.raw: 3 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
3 large carrots, cut into large rough chunks
1 1/2 cups uncooked jasmine rice, cooked (or cauliflower rice with finely chopped cabbage)
ingredients.note: or cauliflower rice with finely chopped cabbage

steps: Braise: heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a medium lidded Dutch oven over medium heat for a minute or two. Add 2 tbsp curry paste and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the beef, stir to coat in the paste, and brown lightly. Add the broth, turn the heat up and bring to a simmer.
Cover, turn off the burner, and braise in the oven for 90 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Lift the beef into a bowl. Set the Dutch oven over medium-high heat and reduce the cooking liquid by about half.
Curry: while that reduces, heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a second large lidded pot over medium heat. Stir-fry 3 tbsp curry paste until fragrant.
Add half a can of coconut cream and simmer, stirring often, until it bubbles and the oil turns red.
Add the reduced braising liquid, the remaining coconut cream, the beef, potatoes, carrots and lime leaves. Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat to medium and simmer 30 minutes.
Uncover, add the fish sauce, sugar, tamarind and peanuts, and cook 15 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender. Taste; if too salty, add water 1/4 cup at a time. Remove the lime leaves.
Serve over rice (or the cabbage and cauliflower rice), topped with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
tips: "Crack" the coconut cream: cook it until the oil separates and turns red before adding the rest of the liquid.
The blog lists 1/3 cup peanuts; the reel shows 1/2 cup. Either works.
The creator's low-carb swap: finely chopped cabbage and cauliflower rice stir-fried in a little olive oil with salt and pepper.

references.title: How to Make the Best Thai Massaman Curry
references.usedFor: confirmed amounts, can size, cut of beef, braise and reduce method, 4 servings, salt adjustment
